Al Jazeera, "Bulgarians vote for president in shadow of Russia's war on Ukraine". Published 25 Oct 2026. Retrieved via WebFetch 17:40 GMT 25 Oct 2026. Exact JSON-LD minute not returned by the fetch — treat the publication time as "25 October" only, not a minute.

WHY THIS MATTERS TONIGHT: THERE IS A THIRD ELECTION TODAY AND WE DID NOT CARRY IT THIS MORNING. Our 08:22 diary item named only Serbia and Brazil. Bulgaria voted today too, and unlike the other two its polls HAVE ALREADY CLOSED by your publication slot.

POLL TIMES — THE KEY TIMING FACT
- Polls opened 7am local, which Al Jazeera gives as 05:00 GMT.
- Polls CLOSED 8pm local, which Al Jazeera gives as 18:00 GMT.
- So at a 19:15 GMT publication, Bulgarian polls have been shut for about an hour and 15 minutes. If anything is declared or exit-polled today, Bulgaria is where it will be — not Serbia (closes 19:00 GMT, first indications about 21:00 GMT) and not Brazil (closes 20:00 GMT).
- Bulgaria is on EET (UTC+2) after the EU clock change; 7am to 8pm local maps to 05:00-18:00 GMT, consistent with Al Jazeera's own conversions.

HARD FIGURES
- 27 candidates on the ballot.
- 6.6 million registered voters.
- A first-round winner needs MORE THAN 50 PERCENT of votes cast, and turnout must also exceed 50 percent of registered voters.
- Turnout was expected to be LESS THAN 40 PERCENT, which makes a run-off on 1 NOVEMBER the expected outcome. EXPECTED, not known. Do not write that a run-off has been triggered unless you have a figure.
- Pre-election polling, Alpha Research via Al Jazeera: Iotova 41 percent, Gyurov 28 percent. A second rendering in approved-domain search results gives RANGES: Iotova 40-45 percent, Gyurov 25-30 percent. Use the Alpha Research point figures or the ranges, attributed — never a blend.
- This is Bulgaria's eighth or later trip to the polls in five years (Al Jazeera's April 2026 piece was headlined "Bulgarians head to polls for eighth time in five years"). Do not print a precise count tonight.

THE TWO LEADING CANDIDATES
- Iliana Iotova, 61, the incumbent. ROLE CONFLICT — DO NOT GUESS: Al Jazeera's piece calls her "President Iliana Iotova"; the Guardian's Ukraine briefing of 02:37 GMT today calls her "acting president Iliana Iotova". Both are approved sources and they differ. Safest form: "the incumbent, Iliana Iotova". Background from the search layer, unverified: Rumen Radev resigned the presidency in January 2026 and Iotova, his vice-president, succeeded him; Radev later became prime minister. I did NOT open a dated article confirming that chain, so do not print it.
- Andrey Gyurov, 50, former caretaker prime minister, backed by pro-Western reformist parties, has long expressed support for Ukraine and signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv while premier.
- Iotova is backed by Radev; both have called for a diplomatic end to the war.

NAMED QUOTES
- Andrey Gyurov, former caretaker prime minister and candidate: "I want Bulgaria to have a voice of its own in Europe, a reliable NATO ally".
- Iliana Iotova, the incumbent: "The truth is, we are all the ones who are most exhausted".
- Rumen Radev, described by Al Jazeera as Bulgarian Prime Minister, on the Black Sea ship attacks: their outcome "benefits the Russian Federation". HE STOPPED SHORT OF BLAMING RUSSIA EXPLICITLY. Label this precisely — it is a pointed non-accusation, and that is the story.

THE BLACK SEA SHIPPING ANGLE — THE REASON THIS IS A GEOPOLITICAL ITEM
- A series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast "likely killed about two dozen international seafarers" (Guardian's Ukraine briefing, 02:37 GMT today, uses "likely killed about two-dozen"). Al Jazeera gives "approximately two dozen".
- BOTH FIGURES ARE HEDGED ("likely", "approximately"). Do not harden it. Write "about two dozen" and keep the hedge.
- The attacks drew international condemnation and raised concern about the reach of Russia's war on Ukraine. Ukraine's president has blamed Russia for an earlier attack on two vessels (NBC headline, early October). Russia has not been shown to have accepted responsibility in anything I read.
